symbols.name: d
symbols.def: A probability law selected before outcomes are observed.

symbols.name: z
symbols.def: The assignment drawn from \(d\), with \(z_i=+1\) for treatment and \(z_i=-1\) for control.

symbols.name: treatment_label
symbols.def: A label indexing the two fixed potential outcomes.

symbols.name: Y_i_obs
symbols.def: The outcome recorded for unit \(i\) after the assignment is drawn.

symbols.name: mu
symbols.def: Let \(m_i=\{y_i(1)+y_i(0)\}/2\); then \(\mu=P_Hm\in H_n\) is its centered component.

symbols.name: S
symbols.space: \(\{L:L\text{ is a linear subspace of }H_n,\ 1\leq\dim L\leq n-1\}\)
symbols.def: The span generated from the external prognostic score matrix after centering, known before assignment.

symbols.name: rho
symbols.def: A free parameter indexing the oracle class through the restriction \(\rho_{\mu}(S)\geq\rho\); it is not a functional of the score matrix.

symbols.name: rho_star_S
symbols.def: \(\rho^*(S)=\inf\{\rho\in[0,1]:V^*(\rho;S)<V_{\mathrm{CRD}}(\rho;S)\}\), with value \(1\) when the set is empty.

symbols.name: d_reg
symbols.def: A design selected without committing to a value of the free lower-bound index \(\rho\) and evaluated by additive oracle regret.

symbols.name: d_pair_4
symbols.def: The law assigning probability \(1/4\) to each element of \(\{\pm(1,-1,1,-1)^\top,\ \pm(1,-1,-1,1)^\top\}\).

symbols.name: S_partition
symbols.space: \(\{L:L\text{ is a block-constant linear subspace of }H_n\}\)
symbols.def: For a partition \(\mathcal P=(G_1,\ldots,G_B)\) of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\), \(S_{\mathcal P}=\{x\in H_n:x_i=x_{i'}\text{ whenever }i,i'\in G_j\text{ for some }j\}\).

symbols.name: S_B
symbols.def: For a fixed partition into \(B\) equal blocks of even size \(m=n/B\), write \(S_B=S_{\mathcal P}\).

symbols.name: S_pair
symbols.def: \(S_{\mathrm{pair}}=\{x\in H_n:x_{2j-1}=x_{2j},\ j=1,\ldots,n/2\}\); equivalently, it is the homogeneous partition space \(S_{n/2}\) with block size \(m=2\).

symbols.name: G_Pi
symbols.def: For block sizes \(m_j=|G_j|\), let \(\mathcal R_{\mathcal P}=\{r\in\mathbb Z^B:r_j\in\{-m_j,-m_j+2,\ldots,m_j\},\ \sum_jr_j=0\}\) and \(\mathcal G_{\mathcal P}=\operatorname{conv}\{rr^\top:r\in\mathcal R_{\mathcal P}\}\).

assumptions.condition: The array \(\{y_i(0),y_i(1):i=1,\ldots,n\}\) is fixed with respect to the assignment law \(d\).

definitions.name: Exact balanced covariance hull
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal C_n=\operatorname{conv}\{zz^\top:z\in\mathcal Z_n\}\), represented by weights on sign-pairs \(\{z,-z\}\).

definitions.name: Realized score quality
definitions.construction: For each specified nonzero \(\mu\in H_n\), \(\rho_{\mu}(S)=\|P_S\mu\|_2/\|\mu\|_2\); the free oracle index \(\rho\in[0,1]\) imposes the lower-bound condition \(\rho_{\mu}(S)\geq\rho\).

definitions.name: Admissibility and threshold invariants
definitions.construction: \(\kappa(S)=\min_{A\in\mathcal C_n}\lambda_{\max}(P_SAP_S\mid S)\) and \(\gamma(S)=\inf_{A\in\mathcal C_n,\eta>0}\{\lambda_{\max}(A+\eta P_S\mid H_n)-c_n\}/\eta\).

definitions.name: Compactified spectral-regret handle
definitions.construction: Put \(s=\rho^2\). For \(A\in\mathcal C_n\) and finite \(\eta\geq0\), define \(F_{A,s}(\eta)=\lambda_{\max}(A+\eta P_S\mid H_n)-\eta s\) and use \(\inf_{\eta\geq0}F_{A,s}(\eta)\). Under \(h=(1+\eta)^{-1}\), adjoin \(h=0\) with boundary value \(+\infty\) when \(s<1\) and \(\lambda_{\max}(P_SAP_S\mid S)\) when \(s=1\). The finite-multiplier robust regret epigraph is interpreted through this value closure; it does not assert an inner optimizer at finite \(\eta\). The balanced-cut-hull support oracle, active-simplex faces, and eigenvalue-crossing cells give the finite real-algebraic handle for \(R^*(n,S)\) and \(d_{\mathrm{reg}}\).

definitions.name: Partition score geometry and homogeneous even-block specialization
definitions.construction:
Let \(\mathcal P=(G_1,\ldots,G_B)\) be a partition of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\), with \(B\geq2\) and \(m_j=|G_j|\). Define
\[
S_{\mathcal P}=\{x\in H_n:x_i=x_{i'}\text{ whenever }i,i'\in G_j\text{ for some }j\}.
\]
For a fixed homogeneous partition into \(B\) equal blocks of even size \(m=n/B\), write \(S_B=S_{\mathcal P}\). The pair partition has \(B=n/2\), \(m=2\), \(G_j=\{2j-1,2j\}\), and \(S_{\mathrm{pair}}=S_{n/2}\).

definitions.name: Four-unit score basis and balanced sign-pair mixture
definitions.construction: Set \(u_4=2^{-1}(1,1,-1,-1)^\top\) and \(S_4=\operatorname{span}\{u_4\}\). Define \(d_{\mathrm{pair},4}\) by probability \(1/4\) on each assignment in \(\{\pm(1,-1,1,-1)^\top,\ \pm(1,-1,-1,1)^\top\}\); its covariance is \(A_{\mathrm{pair},4}=\begin{pmatrix}1&-1&0&0\\-1&1&0&0\\0&0&1&-1\\0&0&-1&1\end{pmatrix}\).

definitions.name: Partition block-sum moment polytope and orbit covariance
definitions.construction:
For a partition \(\mathcal P=(G_1,\ldots,G_B)\) with block sizes \(m_j=|G_j|\), define the feasible block-sum lattice and its second-moment polytope by
\[
\mathcal R_{\mathcal P}
=\left\{r\in\mathbb Z^B:r_j\in\{-m_j,-m_j+2,\ldots,m_j\},\ \sum_{j=1}^B r_j=0\right\},
\qquad
\mathcal G_{\mathcal P}=\operatorname{conv}\{rr^\top:r\in\mathcal R_{\mathcal P}\}.
\]
Let \(W=[\mathbf 1_{G_1}\ \cdots\ \mathbf 1_{G_B}]\), let \(D=\operatorname{diag}(m_1,\ldots,m_B)\), and let \(P_j=I_{G_j}-m_j^{-1}\mathbf 1_{G_j}\mathbf 1_{G_j}^\top\) be embedded in the coordinates of block \(G_j\). For \(G\in\mathcal G_{\mathcal P}\), define
\[
A_{\mathcal P}(G)
=WD^{-1}GD^{-1}W^\top
+\sum_{j:m_j>1}\frac{m_j^2-G_{jj}}{m_j(m_j-1)}P_j.
\]
This formula defines the orbit-covariance candidate used by the reduced unequal-block problem; its realizability and the exactness of the orbit reduction are theorem conclusions, not part of this construction.

statements.statement: For every \(d\in\mathcal D_n\), the estimator \(\widehat\tau_d\) is design-unbiased for \(\tau_n\) and obeys \[\mathbb E_d[(\widehat\tau_d-\tau_n)^2]=\frac{4}{n^2}\mu^\top A_d\mu.\]
statements.justification: This identity turns the design problem into an exact quadratic-risk problem with assignment as the only source of randomness.
statements.gap: HarshawSavjeSpielmanZhang2024, Lemma 1, gives the corresponding covariance identity; the present lemma fixes the balanced difference-in-means normalization used by the new oracle.
statements.consumer: The exact value, admissibility frontier, and regret statements all use this equality to translate their covariance criteria into SATE mean squared error.

statements.statement: The covariance image of \(\mathcal D_n\) is exactly \(\mathcal C_n\): \[\{A_d:d\in\mathcal D_n\}=\operatorname{conv}\{zz^\top:z\in\mathcal Z_n\}.\] In particular, every convex representation can be symmetrized over \(\{z,-z\}\) to yield a mean-zero attaining design without changing its covariance.
statements.justification: This is the implementability bridge that rules out fictitious positive-semidefinite covariance solutions.
statements.gap: HuberMaric2019, p. 5, Theorem 2, characterizes symmetric Bernoulli correlations through the cut polytope, but does not impose the fixed-treatment-count support \(\mathcal Z_n\) or connect it to SATE risk.
statements.consumer: An experimenter can convert every optimizer in the later finite program into an actual balanced randomization distribution.

statements.statement:
For every \(A\in\mathcal C_n\) and \(\rho\in[0,1]\), the nonconvex spherical-shell adversary has the rank-one-exact lift and scalar dual
\[
q_\rho(A;S)=\max_{X\in\mathcal X_\rho(S)}\operatorname{tr}(AX)
=\inf_{\eta\geq0}\left\{\lambda_{\max}(A+\eta P_S\mid H_n)-\eta\rho^2\right\}.
\]
Moreover, the lifted maximum admits a rank-one optimizer. Put \(s=\rho^2\) and, on the one-point compactification \([0,\infty]\), define
\[
\overline F_{A,s}(\eta)=\lambda_{\max}(A+\eta P_S\mid H_n)-\eta s
\quad(\eta<\infty),
\]
with \(\overline F_{A,s}(\infty)=+\infty\) for \(s<1\), and
\[
\overline F_{A,1}(\infty)=\lambda_{\max}(P_SAP_S\mid S).
\]
Then
\[
q_\rho(A;S)=\min_{\eta\in[0,\infty]}\overline F_{A,s}(\eta).
\]
If \(\rho<1\), the infimum over finite \(\eta\) is attained; at \(\rho=1\), it may be attained only at \(\eta=\infty\).
statements.proof_tex:
\textit{Proof.}
Write \(s=\rho^2\), and let
\[
\mathcal E_H=\{X\succeq0:X=P_HXP_H,\ \operatorname{tr}(X)=1\}.
\]
The set
\[
K_s=\{X\in\mathcal E_H:\operatorname{tr}(P_SX)\geq s\}
=\mathcal X_\rho(S)
\]
is nonempty and compact: if \(x\) is any unit vector in \(S\), then \(xx^\top\in K_s\). Every unit vector \(u\in H_n\) feasible for \(q_\rho(A;S)\) gives the feasible rank-one matrix \(X=uu^\top\), and \(\operatorname{tr}(AX)=u^\top Au\).

We prove the converse by identifying the extreme points relevant to the lifted maximum. A linear functional on the compact convex set \(K_s\) has an extreme-point maximizer. Suppose that an extreme point \(X\) has rank \(r\geq2\), and let \(R=\operatorname{range}(X)\subseteq H_n\). The vector space of symmetric operators on \(R\) has dimension \(r(r+1)/2\geq3\). If the score constraint is active, there is therefore a nonzero symmetric operator \(D\), supported on \(R\), such that
\[
\operatorname{tr}(D)=0,
\qquad
\operatorname{tr}(P_SD)=0,
\]
because these are at most two homogeneous linear equations. If the score constraint is inactive, choose a nonzero such \(D\) subject only to \(\operatorname{tr}(D)=0\). Since \(X\) is positive definite on \(R\), for all sufficiently small \(\epsilon>0\), both \(X+\epsilon D\) and \(X-\epsilon D\) are positive semidefinite. They retain the support and trace restrictions. In the active case they retain the score equality, and in the inactive case the strict slack persists for sufficiently small \(\epsilon\). Thus \(X\) is the midpoint of two distinct points of \(K_s\), contradicting extremality. Every extreme point is consequently rank one. A rank-one point of \(K_s\) is \(uu^\top\) for a unit \(u\in H_n\) satisfying \(u^\top P_Su\geq s\). Hence
\[
q_\rho(A;S)=\max_{X\in K_s}\operatorname{tr}(AX),
\]
and the maximum has a rank-one optimizer.

We next derive the scalar dual without assuming a limit law or a dual-attainment statement. For \(K>0\), define
\[
L(X,\eta)=\operatorname{tr}(AX)+\eta\{\operatorname{tr}(P_SX)-s\},
\qquad X\in\mathcal E_H,\quad 0\leq\eta\leq K.
\]
We first verify the elementary compact bilinear minimax identity
\[
\max_{X\in\mathcal E_H}\min_{0\leq\eta\leq K}L(X,\eta)
=\min_{0\leq\eta\leq K}\max_{X\in\mathcal E_H}L(X,\eta).
\tag{1}
\]
Indeed, the set
\[
\mathcal G=\{(L(X,0),L(X,K)):X\in\mathcal E_H\}\subset\mathbb R^2
\]
is compact and convex. If \(r>\max_X\min\{L(X,0),L(X,K)\}\), then \(\mathcal G\) is disjoint from \([r,\infty)^2\). Finite-dimensional strong separation gives nonnegative weights \(a_0,a_K\), normalized so that \(a_0+a_K=1\), for which
\[
\max_{X\in\mathcal E_H}\{a_0L(X,0)+a_KL(X,K)\}<r.
\]
The expression in braces is \(L(X,a_KK)\). Letting \(r\) decrease to the left side of (1) proves the nontrivial inequality in (1); the reverse inequality is the elementary weak-minimax inequality.

Because \(L\) is affine in \(\eta\), the left side of (1) equals
\[
\Phi_K
=\max_{X\in\mathcal E_H}
\left[\operatorname{tr}(AX)-K\{s-\operatorname{tr}(P_SX)\}_+\right].
\tag{2}
\]
The sequence \(\Phi_K\) decreases as \(K\) increases and is bounded below by the constrained maximum over \(K_s\). Choose a maximizer \(X_K\) in (2). Since \(\operatorname{tr}(AX)\) is uniformly bounded on \(\mathcal E_H\), comparison with any fixed member of \(K_s\) gives
\[
\{s-\operatorname{tr}(P_SX_K)\}_+=O(K^{-1}).
\]
Every cluster point of \(X_K\) is therefore in \(K_s\). Along a convergent subsequence, (2) and continuity give
\[
\limsup_{K\to\infty}\Phi_K
\leq\max_{X\in K_s}\operatorname{tr}(AX).
\]
The reverse inequality holds for every \(K\), so \(\Phi_K\) converges to the lifted primal value.

For fixed \(\eta\), the spectral decomposition of the symmetric operator \(A+\eta P_S\) on \(H_n\) gives
\[
\max_{X\in\mathcal E_H}L(X,\eta)
=\lambda_{\max}(A+\eta P_S\mid H_n)-\eta s.
\]
Taking \(K\to\infty\) on the right side of (1) consequently proves
\[
\max_{X\in K_s}\operatorname{tr}(AX)
=\inf_{\eta\geq0}
\{\lambda_{\max}(A+\eta P_S\mid H_n)-\eta s\}.
\tag{3}
\]

It remains to establish the asserted boundary and attainment facts. Since \(A\in\mathcal C_n\), it is positive semidefinite. Testing \(A+\eta P_S\) on any unit vector in \(S\) gives
\[
\lambda_{\max}(A+\eta P_S\mid H_n)-\eta s
\geq\eta(1-s).
\]
Thus, for \(s<1\), the continuous finite-multiplier objective tends to \(+\infty\) as \(\eta\to\infty\), so its infimum is attained at a finite \(\eta\).

Now let \(s=1\). If \(X\in K_1\), then
\[
\operatorname{tr}\{(P_H-P_S)X\}
=\operatorname{tr}(X)-\operatorname{tr}(P_SX)=0.
\]
Positive semidefiniteness forces \(X=P_SXP_S\). Therefore
\[
q_1(A;S)=c,
\qquad
c:=\lambda_{\max}(P_SAP_S\mid S).
\tag{4}
\]
Weak duality in (3) gives
\[
\lambda_{\max}(A+\eta P_S\mid H_n)-\eta\geq c
\quad\text{for every finite }\eta.
\tag{5}
\]
To obtain the matching limit, put \(T=H_n\cap S^\perp\) and \(L_A=\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\). For a unit vector \(u=x+y\), with \(x\in S\), \(y\in T\), and \(b=\|y\|_2\), the Rayleigh quotient and (4) imply, for \(\eta>L_A\),
\[
u^\top(A+\eta P_S)u-\eta
\leq c+2L_Ab-(\eta-L_A)b^2
\leq c+\frac{L_A^2}{\eta-L_A}.
\]
When \(T=\{0\}\), the same conclusion is immediate with equality. Taking the supremum over unit \(u\), combining with (5), and sending \(\eta\to\infty\) yields
\[
\lambda_{\max}(A+\eta P_S\mid H_n)-\eta
\longrightarrow\lambda_{\max}(P_SAP_S\mid S).
\]
Consequently the displayed definition of \(\overline F_{A,s}(\infty)\) is exactly the extended-real limit of the finite-multiplier objective. The one-point compactification therefore turns (3) into the stated attained minimum. At \(s=1\), the example in which the finite objective decreases strictly to (4) shows why only the compactified endpoint, rather than a finite multiplier, can be guaranteed. \(\square\)
statements.justification: The exact lift is the technical move that makes the quality cone solvable without relaxing away its worst-case outcome vector.
statements.gap: Kallus2018OptimalBalance and Kallus2021Randomization reduce ellipsoidal classes to largest eigenvalues; no located result supplies this exact two-constraint lift for a lower score-energy shell.
statements.consumer: The dual exposes score quality as a scalar slope and yields both the critical-quality formula and the regret breakpoint handle.

statements.statement: For every \(\rho\in[0,1]\), \[v^*(\rho;S)=\min_{A\in\mathcal C_n}\max_{X\in\mathcal X_\rho(S)}\operatorname{tr}(AX)=\max_{X\in\mathcal X_\rho(S)}\min_{z\in\mathcal Z_n}z^\top Xz.\] Equivalently, \(v^*(\rho;S)\) is the optimum of \[\max_{X,t}\ t\quad\text{subject to}\quad X\in\mathcal X_\rho(S),\quad t\leq z^\top Xz\ \text{for every }z\in\mathcal Z_n.\] The dual yields weights on balanced sign-pairs defining an attaining \(d^*_{\rho,S}\in\mathcal D_n\), and every \(d\in\mathcal D_n\) satisfies \[\sup_{\mu\in\mathcal Y(\rho,M;S)}\mathbb E_d[(\widehat\tau_d-\tau_n)^2]\geq V^*(\rho;S),\] with equality for \(d^*_{\rho,S}\).
statements.justification: This is the exact design and matching converse over the full discrete design class, not an elliptope relaxation or a candidate procedure.
statements.gap: Kallus2021Randomization, Section 5, identifies the generic mixed-strategy optimal design for a specified conditional-mean class. The theorem-level delta here is the solution of the nonellipsoidal lower score-energy shell: a rank-one-exact lift, an explicit finite saddle value over the balanced cut hull, sign-pair recovery of an attaining design, and a matching converse over every balanced mean-zero law. HarshawSavjeSpielmanZhang2024 instead provides bounds for one named design.
statements.consumer: Trial designers with an externally trained score can enumerate or column-generate the oracle assignment mixture and report a certified worst-case SATE risk.

statements.statement:
The following conditions are equivalent:
\[
(i)\ S\in\mathfrak A_n,
\qquad
(ii)\ \kappa(S)<c_n,
\qquad
(iii)\ \gamma(S)<1.
\]
When these conditions hold, \(\rho^*(S)=\sqrt{\gamma(S)}\); otherwise \(\rho^*(S)=1\).  Put \(p=\dim(S)\), \(\beta=p/(n-1)\), and \(\ell_i=(P_S)_{ii}\).  For \(t\in[\beta,1]\), define
\[
d_i(t)=\frac{n-1}{n}t-\ell_i
\]
and
\[
U(\ell)=\min\left\{
t\in[\beta,1]:\ d_i(t)\geq0\ \text{for every }i,\quad
2\max_i\sqrt{d_i(t)}\leq\sum_{i=1}^n\sqrt{d_i(t)}
\right\}.
\]
Then the critical squared quality is determined exactly by the score leverage profile:
\[
\gamma(S)
=\min_{\substack{K=K^\top,\ K\mathbf1_n=0\\
\operatorname{diag}(K)=\operatorname{diag}(P_S)}}
\lambda_{\max}(K\mid H_n)
=U\!\left(\operatorname{diag}(P_S)\right).
\]
In particular, the sharp leverage and dimension bounds are
\[
\gamma(S)\geq\frac{n}{n-1}\max_i\ell_i
\geq\frac{p}{n-1},
\]
and equality in the dimension bound holds if and only if
\[
\operatorname{diag}(P_S)=\frac{p}{n}(1,\ldots,1)^\top.
\]
At \(n=4\), the rank-one leverage profiles
\[
\left(\tfrac14,\tfrac14,\tfrac14,\tfrac14\right),\qquad
\left(\tfrac16,\tfrac16,0,\tfrac23\right),\qquad
\left(\tfrac34,\tfrac1{12},\tfrac1{12},\tfrac1{12}\right)
\]
have exact threshold invariants \(1/3\), \(8/9\), and \(1\), respectively.

Consequently, for every \(S\),
\[
\{\rho^*(S)\}^2\geq\frac{p}{n-1},
\]
where the convention \(\rho^*(S)=1\) applies off \(\mathfrak A_n\), and
\[
V^*(\rho;S)<V_{\mathrm{CRD}}(\rho;S)
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\rho^2>\gamma(S)\geq\frac{n}{n-1}\max_i\ell_i
\geq\frac{p}{n-1}.
\]
Given a basis matrix for \(S\), forming \(P_S\) and performing a one-dimensional feasibility search computes \(\gamma(S)\) and \(\rho^*(S)\) from the score matrix alone.  Enumeration of \(\mathcal Z_n\) and semidefinite optimization compute \(\kappa(S)\) and an \(\varepsilon\)-optimal implementable assignment mixture.
statements.justification: The theorem converts the design-stage admissibility question into an exact one-dimensional functional of the score projector diagonal, while retaining the attaining full-hull oracle design and matching causal-risk converse.
statements.gap: Prior formulations did not show that the projector leverage profile alone determines the critical squared quality exactly, rather than merely bounding it, inside the realizable balanced covariance hull.
statements.consumer: A protocol author can compute \(\rho^*(S)\) from the score matrix without enumerating assignments, screen design-useless geometries, and then solve the finite oracle program only for the desired quality-specific design.

statements.statement:
If \(S=H_n\), then \(v^*(\rho;S)=c_n\) for every \(\rho\in[0,1]\), so \(S\notin\mathfrak A_n\). Let \(r_1=(1,0,\ldots,0)^\top\), and define the singleton-versus-rest score space and its normalized basis by
\[
S_{\mathrm{out}}=\operatorname{span}\{P_Hr_1\},
\qquad
u_{\mathrm{out}}=\frac{P_Hr_1}{\|P_Hr_1\|_2}.
\]
For every \(z\in\mathcal Z_n\), \((u_{\mathrm{out}}^\top z)^2=c_n\), and consequently
\[
v^*(\rho;S_{\mathrm{out}})=c_n\quad(0\leq\rho\leq1),
\qquad
\kappa(S_{\mathrm{out}})=c_n,
\qquad
\gamma(S_{\mathrm{out}})=1,
\qquad
S_{\mathrm{out}}\notin\mathfrak A_n.
\]
At \(n=4\), define
\[
u_{\mathrm{mid}}=6^{-1/2}(1,1,0,-2)^\top,
\qquad
S_{\mathrm{mid}}=\operatorname{span}\{u_{\mathrm{mid}}\}.
\]
Then
\[
\kappa(S_{\mathrm{mid}})=\frac23,
\qquad
\gamma(S_{\mathrm{mid}})=\frac89,
\qquad
\rho^*(S_{\mathrm{mid}})=\frac{2\sqrt2}{3},
\qquad
S_{\mathrm{mid}}\in\mathfrak A_4.
\]
For the worked equal-leverage basis \(u_4=2^{-1}(1,1,-1,-1)^\top\) and \(S_4=\operatorname{span}\{u_4\}=S_{\mathrm{pair}}\), the displayed balanced sign-pair mixture \(d_{\mathrm{pair},4}\) has covariance \(A_{\mathrm{pair},4}\) and satisfies
\[
v^*(\rho;S_4)=\min\left\{\frac43,\ 2(1-\rho^2)\right\},
\qquad
\kappa(S_4)=0,
\qquad
\gamma(S_4)=\frac13,
\qquad
\rho^*(S_4)=\frac1{\sqrt3}.
\]
Complete randomization attains the first branch for \(\rho\leq1/\sqrt3\), while \(d_{\mathrm{pair},4}\) attains the second branch for \(\rho\geq1/\sqrt3\). Thus the three rank-one four-unit spaces \(S_4\), \(S_{\mathrm{mid}}\), and \(S_{\mathrm{out}}\) have threshold invariants \(1/3\), \(8/9\), and \(1\), respectively, so the variational invariant contains information not determined by dimension alone. More generally, independent fair orientations within fixed pairs give \(\kappa(S_{\mathrm{pair}})=0\), so \(S_{\mathrm{pair}}\in\mathfrak A_n\). At \(n=8\) and \(M=1\), \(V^*(1;S_{\mathrm{pair}})=0\) while \(V_{\mathrm{CRD}}(1;S_{\mathrm{pair}})=4/7\).
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Suppose first that \(S=H_n\). The score constraint is then automatic for every unit vector in \(H_n\), and hence
\[
q_\rho(A;H_n)=\lambda_{\max}(A\mid H_n).
\tag{1}
\]
Every \(A\in\mathcal C_n\) is positive semidefinite, annihilates \(\mathbf1_n\), and has trace \(n\). Therefore
\[
\lambda_{\max}(A\mid H_n)\geq\frac{n}{n-1}=c_n.
\tag{2}
\]
Complete randomization has covariance \(c_nP_H\), so \((1)\)--\((2)\) give \(v^*(\rho;H_n)=c_n\) for every \(\rho\), and thus \(H_n\notin\mathfrak A_n\).

For the singleton-versus-rest geometry, put \(w=P_Hr_1\) and \(u_{\mathrm{out}}=w/\|w\|_2\), consistently with the statement. Since
\[
w=r_1-\frac1n\mathbf1_n,
\qquad
\|w\|_2^2=r_1^\top P_Hr_1=1-\frac1n=\frac{n-1}{n},
\tag{3}
\]
every balanced assignment \(z\in\mathcal Z_n\) satisfies
\[
(u_{\mathrm{out}}^\top z)^2
=\frac{(r_1^\top z)^2}{\|w\|_2^2}
=\frac{n}{n-1}=c_n,
\tag{4}
\]
because \(\mathbf1_n^\top z=0\) and \(z_1^2=1\). For any \(A\in\mathcal C_n\), convex averaging of \((4)\) gives
\[
u_{\mathrm{out}}^\top Au_{\mathrm{out}}=c_n.
\tag{5}
\]
The vector \(u_{\mathrm{out}}\) lies in \(S_{\mathrm{out}}\), so it is feasible for every quality level. Thus \((5)\) implies \(q_\rho(A;S_{\mathrm{out}})\geq c_n\) for every \(A\), while complete randomization attains equality. Therefore
\[
v^*(\rho;S_{\mathrm{out}})=c_n
\qquad(0\leq\rho\leq1).
\tag{6}
\]
Because \(S_{\mathrm{out}}\) is one-dimensional, equation \((5)\) also gives \(\kappa(S_{\mathrm{out}})=c_n\). The admissibility-frontier theorem then gives \(S_{\mathrm{out}}\notin\mathfrak A_n\) and \(\gamma(S_{\mathrm{out}})=1\).

We next prove the intermediate four-unit calculation by an exact enumeration. Choose the three balanced sign-pair representatives
\[
z^{(1)}=(1,1,-1,-1)^\top,
\quad
z^{(2)}=(1,-1,1,-1)^\top,
\quad
z^{(3)}=(1,-1,-1,1)^\top,
\tag{7}
\]
and put \(e_j=z^{(j)}/2\). Every balanced four-unit assignment is one of \(\pm z^{(1)},\pm z^{(2)},\pm z^{(3)}\), and direct multiplication gives \(e_j^\top e_\ell=\mathbf1\{j=\ell\}\). Hence \((e_1,e_2,e_3)\) is an orthonormal basis of \(H_4\), and every \(A\in\mathcal C_4\) is diagonal in this basis with eigenvalues
\[
\lambda_j=4a_j\geq0,
\qquad
\lambda_1+\lambda_2+\lambda_3=4,
\tag{8}
\]
for some \((a_1,a_2,a_3)\) in the probability simplex. The coordinates of \(u_{\mathrm{mid}}\) are
\[
(e_1^\top u_{\mathrm{mid}},e_2^\top u_{\mathrm{mid}},e_3^\top u_{\mathrm{mid}})
=\left(\sqrt{\frac23},\sqrt{\frac16},-\sqrt{\frac16}\right).
\tag{9}
\]
It follows from \((8)\)--\((9)\) that
\[
u_{\mathrm{mid}}^\top Au_{\mathrm{mid}}
=\frac23\lambda_1+\frac16\lambda_2+\frac16\lambda_3
\geq\frac23.
\tag{10}
\]
Equality in \((10)\) is attained, for example, by \((\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\lambda_3)=(0,4,0)\), which is the feasible covariance \(z^{(2)}z^{(2)\top}\). Since \(S_{\mathrm{mid}}\) is one-dimensional, this proves \(\kappa(S_{\mathrm{mid}})=2/3\) with both a lower-bound certificate and an attaining covariance.

It remains to calculate \(\gamma(S_{\mathrm{mid}})\). Reverse the sign of \(e_3\); this preserves every diagonal representation in \((8)\) and changes the coordinate vector in \((9)\) to
\[
c=\frac1{\sqrt6}(2,1,1)^\top.
\tag{11}
\]
Let \(r=3^{-1/2}(1,1,1)^\top\). For every feasible diagonal covariance \(A=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\lambda_3)\) in this basis and every \(\eta>0\), the Rayleigh quotient at \(r\) gives
\[
\lambda_{\max}(A+\eta P_{S_{\mathrm{mid}}}\mid H_4)
\geq r^\top\{A+\eta cc^\top\}r
=\frac{\lambda_1+\lambda_2+\lambda_3}{3}
+\eta(r^\top c)^2
=\frac43+\frac89\eta.
\tag{12}
\]
Thus every quotient defining \(\gamma(S_{\mathrm{mid}})\) is at least \(8/9\).

For the matching attainment, fix any \(0<\eta\leq3\) and choose the feasible covariance whose eigenvalues in the sign-adjusted cut basis are
\[
\lambda_1=\frac43-\frac49\eta,
\qquad
\lambda_2=\lambda_3=\frac43+\frac29\eta.
\tag{13}
\]
They are nonnegative and sum to four, so \((8)\) shows that this covariance belongs to \(\mathcal C_4\). Direct multiplication shows that the three eigenvalues of \(A+\eta cc^\top\) are
\[
\frac43+\frac89\eta,
\qquad
\frac43+\frac29\eta,
\qquad
\frac43-\frac19\eta,
\tag{14}
\]
with respective eigenvectors proportional to \((1,1,1)^\top\), \((0,1,-1)^\top\), and \((-2,1,1)^\top\). The first value in \((14)\) is the largest. Therefore the quotient in the definition of \(\gamma(S_{\mathrm{mid}})\) equals \(8/9\), and \((12)\)--\((14)\) prove
\[
\gamma(S_{\mathrm{mid}})=\frac89.
\tag{15}
\]
Since \(8/9<1\), the admissibility-frontier theorem yields
\[
S_{\mathrm{mid}}\in\mathfrak A_4,
\qquad
\rho^*(S_{\mathrm{mid}})=\sqrt{\frac89}=\frac{2\sqrt2}{3}.
\tag{16}
\]

For the pair geometry, \(\text{lem:pair-space-exact-frontier}\), specialized to homogeneous blocks of size two, gives for every even \(n\geq4\)
\[
v^*(\rho;S_{\mathrm{pair}})
=\min\left\{\frac{n}{n-1},2(1-\rho^2)\right\},
\qquad
\kappa(S_{\mathrm{pair}})=0,
\tag{17}
\]
and
\[
\gamma(S_{\mathrm{pair}})=\frac{n-2}{2(n-1)},
\qquad
\rho^*(S_{\mathrm{pair}})=\sqrt{\frac{n-2}{2(n-1)}}.
\tag{18}
\]
It also identifies complete randomization and independent fair within-pair orientations as the two attaining endpoint designs. At \(n=4\), \((17)\)--\((18)\), together with \(S_4=S_{\mathrm{pair}}\), become
\[
v^*(\rho;S_4)=\min\left\{\frac43,2(1-\rho^2)\right\},
\quad
\kappa(S_4)=0,
\quad
\gamma(S_4)=\frac13,
\quad
\rho^*(S_4)=\frac1{\sqrt3}.
\tag{19}
\]
Moreover, \(P_{S_4}=u_4u_4^\top\) has every diagonal entry equal to \(1/4\), so \(S_4\) is equal leverage and attains the rank-one dimension floor. In contrast, \((15)\) and \((6)\) give the strictly larger rank-one thresholds \(8/9\) and \(1\) for \(S_{\mathrm{mid}}\) and \(S_{\mathrm{out}}\). The two branches in \((19)\) meet at \(\rho^2=1/3\), giving the stated ranges of the attaining designs.

To verify the displayed four-unit law directly, put
\[
a=(1,-1,1,-1)^\top,
\qquad
b=(1,-1,-1,1)^\top.
\]
The support of \(d_{\mathrm{pair},4}\) is \(\{a,-a,b,-b\}\), with probability \(1/4\) on each point. It is balanced and sign symmetric, so it belongs to \(\mathcal D_4\), and
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_{d_{\mathrm{pair},4}}[zz^\top]
&=\frac12aa^\top+\frac12bb^\top\\
&=\begin{pmatrix}
1&-1&0&0\\
-1&1&0&0\\
0&0&1&-1\\
0&0&-1&1
\end{pmatrix}
=A_{\mathrm{pair},4}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{20}
\]
These are exactly the four outcomes of two independent fair pair orientations, so the second branch in \((19)\) is attained by the displayed law. For general even \(n\), \(\kappa(S_{\mathrm{pair}})=0<c_n\), and the admissibility-frontier theorem gives \(S_{\mathrm{pair}}\in\mathfrak A_n\). Finally, at \(n=8\), \(M=1\), and \(\rho=1\),
\[
V^*(1;S_{\mathrm{pair}})
=\frac{4M}{n}v^*(1;S_{\mathrm{pair}})=0,
\qquad
V_{\mathrm{CRD}}(1;S_{\mathrm{pair}})=\frac{4M}{n-1}=\frac47.
\tag{21}
\]
This proves every assertion. \(\square\)
statements.justification: The endpoint reductions give three reproducible four-unit geometries at the same rank: the equal-leverage pair score attains the dimension floor, the intermediate score has exact threshold \(8/9\), and singleton-versus-rest has threshold one and cannot improve on complete randomization.
statements.gap: Matched-pair results alone do not reveal that other rank-one score geometries can have a strict intermediate threshold or be entirely useless over the unrestricted balanced design class; the explicit cut-basis witnesses isolate geometry beyond dimension.
statements.consumer: The explicit four-unit covariance certificates provide unit tests for the cut-hull solver and warn protocol authors that score dimension alone cannot certify a useful restricted design.

statements.statement: Using the spectral-breakpoint handle, characterize \(R^*(n,S)\) by a finite optimization whose constraints and breakpoints are computable from a score basis, construct an attaining \(d_{\mathrm{reg}}\in\mathcal D_n\), and prove a matching lower bound against every single design selected without knowledge of \(\rho\). Determine whether the support of an attaining design can always be chosen from the union of supports of finitely many \(\rho\)-oracle designs.
statements.justification: Score quality is unavailable when randomization is chosen, so oracle optimality alone does not tell an experimenter which design to run.
statements.gap: KapelnerKriegerSklarAzriel2022 tunes a rerandomization threshold using unknown response quantities, while HarshawSavjeSpielmanZhang2024 offers heuristics for an unavailable predictive ratio; neither solves oracle-relative regret over all balanced laws.
statements.consumer: A trial protocol that must be frozen before observing outcomes needs one certified quality-agnostic assignment distribution.

sampling_model.design: A law \(d\in\mathcal D_n\) on exactly balanced sign assignments, selected using only the fixed score subspace \(S\).
sampling_model.units: A fixed finite population of even size \(n\); there is no superpopulation draw.
sampling_model.treatment: Exactly \(n/2\) units receive treatment and \(n/2\) receive control; \(z\sim d\) is the only random object.
sampling_model.overlap: Mean-zero assignment, \(\mathbb E_d[z]=0\), gives marginal treatment probability \(1/2\) for every unit.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None; the score-derived subspace \(S\) is a fixed design-stage primitive. The realized quality \(\rho_{\mu}(S)=\|P_S\mu\|_2/\|\mu\|_2\) depends on fixed potential outcomes, whereas \(\rho\in[0,1]\) is a free lower-bound parameter indexing oracle classes.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The exact design-based mean squared error is a quadratic form in assignment covariance, while the Gram--Schmidt Walk supplies separate finite-sample balance and robustness guarantees.

Section 5 provides the broader mixed-strategy minimax-design framework and a largest-eigenvalue criterion for ellipsoidal conditional-mean classes. It does not derive the lower-score-energy-shell identity \(\gamma(S)=U(\operatorname{diag}(P_S))\) or a leverage-only quality threshold, while the present score-shell theorem does not subsume Kallus's broader outcome-class framework.

The accepted-bank theorem computes a parity-sensitive gap between a two-community block-elliptope relaxation and its realizable randomized plus-or-minus-one covariance slice for an interference objective.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: thm:exact-oracle-saddle solves a different exact-hull game against a score-quality shell; neither theorem subsumes the other.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Page 5, Theorem 2 characterizes symmetric Bernoulli correlation vectors through membership in a cut polytope.
Matched-pair randomization is precision-optimal within the paper's stratified superpopulation design class.
Schuler et al. study analysis-stage linear adjustment using an externally trained prognostic score and show that efficiency gains depend on its predictive accuracy in the trial.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: thm:admissibility-frontier instead studies design-stage balanced randomization under an unknown score-subspace quality index and derives a leverage-only admissibility threshold; neither result subsumes the other.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper studies optimal rerandomization rules within a rerandomization design class.
The paper proves a central limit theorem for the Gram--Schmidt random-walk design.
A rerandomization threshold trades observed balance against unobserved-covariate tail risk using unknown response quantities.
The paper studies minimax-regret sample selection for randomized experiments with heterogeneous subpopulations.
Euclidean rerandomization is minimax robust within a class of quadratic-form rerandomization criteria.
Gaussianized design optimization searches a restricted covariance family by local continuous optimization because the full binary covariance problem is cut-polytope hard.

tldr: An external prognostic score is useful for design only when its realized alignment \(\rho_{\mu}(S)=\|P_S\mu\|_2/\|\mu\|_2\) is high enough to compensate for the off-score risk created by restricted randomization; \(\rho\in[0,1]\) is the free lower-bound parameter indexing this oracle comparison. The paper derives the exact finite-population minimax SATE risk over every balanced mean-zero assignment law by lifting the score-quality shell to a rank-one-exact spectrahedron and optimizing over the true balanced sign covariance hull. The same reduction yields an attaining mixed design, a matching converse, an if-and-only-if admissibility certificate \(\kappa(S)<n/(n-1)\), and the score-matrix-computable threshold \(\rho^*(S)=\sqrt{\gamma(S)}\). A four-unit pair-score basis gives the worked values \(\kappa=0\), \(\gamma=1/3\), and \(\rho^*=1/\sqrt3\) with an explicit attaining sign-pair mixture. The remaining open object is the exact additive regret of one design chosen without knowing which lower bound is warranted.

project_justification.gap: Existing design theory either proves that complete randomization is minimax without predictive structure, optimizes a named restricted design under a chosen tuning parameter, or defines a generic mixed-strategy criterion and evaluates ellipsoidal outcome classes. It does not solve the nonellipsoidal lower score-energy shell, determine its exact fixed-count realizable covariance, or locate the transition below perfect prediction for an arbitrary external-score subspace.
project_justification.niche: The lower score-energy shell is strong enough to make minimax design nondegenerate but weak enough to represent score miscalibration and population shift. Its two quadratic constraints permit an exact lift, while exact balance forces the optimizer to remain in the balanced cut hull.
project_justification.fill: The proposal combines a rank-one-exact semidefinite adversary, minimax duality over balanced sign mixtures, and a compressed spectral certificate to deliver the value, attaining design, converse, admissibility dichotomy, and critical quality using only the score geometry available before randomization.

related_work: HarshawSavjeSpielmanZhang2024 supplies the design-based covariance identity and motivates tuning by predictive quality, but Section 8 of its supplement states that the relevant quality ratio is unavailable at design time. Kallus2018OptimalBalance develops the zero-sum mixed-design architecture and the no-free-lunch benchmark under unstructured outcomes. Kallus2021Randomization, Section 5, defines the generic mixed-strategy optimal design for a specified conditional-mean class and gives a largest-eigenvalue criterion for an ellipsoidal class. The theorem-level delta is not the generic existence of an optimal mixture: it is the rank-one-exact solution of the nonellipsoidal lower score-energy shell, the exact saddle program over the fixed-count balanced cut hull, recovery of an attaining sign-pair law, and the if-and-only-if quality frontier. HuberMaric2019, p. 5, Theorem 2, identifies symmetric Bernoulli correlation vectors with a cut-polytope image; it neither imposes fixed treatment counts nor studies causal risk. Bai2022MatchedPairs gives a scalar-prognosis endpoint within stratified superpopulation designs, not a converse over all fixed-population balanced laws. KapelnerKriegerSklarAzriel2022 shows that rerandomization tuning depends on unknown response features, motivating oracle-relative regret. SchulerWalshHallWalshFisher2022 documents why externally trained score quality can deteriorate under domain shift. SchindlBranson2024 compares quadratic-form rerandomization rules but explicitly leaves comparison with other design classes outside its scope. GuoLiangToulis2025 uses a Gaussianized covariance subclass and local optimization because the full binary covariance geometry is hard; the present exact program keeps the full discrete hull and accepts exponential worst-case computation.
technical_internal_limitation: For \(n=8\) and \(S=S_{\mathrm{pair}}\), the matched-pair design has zero risk on vectors constant within pairs, yet exact enumeration also produces a fixed mean vector with within-pair variation on which its risk is \(1.75\) times the complete-randomization risk. Thus \(V^*(1;S_{\mathrm{pair}})=0\) does not justify matched pairs at lower quality, and no theorem may infer global dominance from perfect-score performance.
honest_scope: The finite-population oracle value, attaining design, full-class converse, admissibility dichotomy, threshold formula, computability by finite enumeration, and endpoint reductions are theorem targets. Polynomial-time computation is not claimed; the balanced cut hull can require exponentially many assignments. The exact finite-breakpoint form of \(R^*(n,S)\), its attaining quality-agnostic design, and any asymptotic growing-rank theory remain open. The sanity reduction \(S=H_n\) returns complete randomization for every quality. For the four-unit pair-score basis, the exact switch from complete randomization to the displayed balanced sign-pair mixture occurs at \(\rho=1/\sqrt3\), while general \(S_{\mathrm{pair}}\) returns the zero-risk matched-pair endpoint at \(\rho=1\).
